Read mouse tracking data

Source: R/tracking.R
read_mousetracking.Rd

Reads the files that the Mouse Tracking component of Task Builder 2 saves for each trial. 'Gorilla' does not put these recordings in the main export but in files of their own, named like 123456-3-9100037-task-ab12-50000037-mousetracking-10-2.csv.

Usage

read_mousetracking(path, x = NULL, zones = NULL, quiet = FALSE)

Arguments

path

Paths to folders, CSV files or ZIP archives. Folders and ZIP archives are searched recursively for files whose names contain -mousetracking-. CSV files named directly are read whatever their name.

x

Optional gorilla_data object from read_gorilla() of the same experiment, used to add the task and screen names.

zones

Names of the zones to assign samples to. All by default.

quiet

If TRUE, no message about files that could not be used is shown.

Value

An object of class gorilla_mousetracking: a list with

mouse

One row per sample, with the participant, node, task, spreadsheet, trial and screen, the kind of sample (type, usually "mouse"), a timer of the browser in milliseconds (timestamp, not a date), the time since the start of the recording in milliseconds (elapsed), the position of the pointer (x, y, x_raw, y_raw) and the zone it is in (zone_id, zone_name).

zones

One row per zone and recording, with the object ID (zone_id), the name, and the edges left, right, bottom and top in normalised coordinates.

files

One row per file read, with its kind and number of rows.

Details

Positions are given in normalised coordinates: 0 to 1 across the area of the task, with the origin at the bottom left, as in the export. Raw coordinates in pixels are kept as x_raw and y_raw; in these, as recorded by the browser, y counts from the top of the window.

Each sample is assigned to the zone of the screen it falls in. When zones overlap, the smallest zone containing the sample wins. Use zones to test only some zones.

The recordings do not say which task they belong to. Pass the main export as x to add task_name, so that the samples can be joined to gorilla_trials() by participant_private_id, tree_node_key, display, trial and screen.

See also

read_eyetracking() for the Eye Tracking component.

Examples

g <- read_gorilla(gorilla_example(), quiet = TRUE)
mouse <- read_mousetracking(gorilla_example(), x = g)
mouse
#> <gorilla_mousetracking>
#> 40 samples from 1 participant in 1 recording; 22.5% in a zone
mouse$mouse
#> # A tibble: 40 × 20
#>    participant_private_id experiment_version tree_node_key task_name spreadsheet
#>    <chr>                               <dbl> <chr>         <chr>     <chr>      
#>  1 9100037                                 3 task-ld2k     Lexical … Spreadshee…
#>  2 9100037                                 3 task-ld2k     Lexical … Spreadshee…
#>  3 9100037                                 3 task-ld2k     Lexical … Spreadshee…
#>  4 9100037                                 3 task-ld2k     Lexical … Spreadshee…
#>  5 9100037                                 3 task-ld2k     Lexical … Spreadshee…
#>  6 9100037                                 3 task-ld2k     Lexical … Spreadshee…
#>  7 9100037                                 3 task-ld2k     Lexical … Spreadshee…
#>  8 9100037                                 3 task-ld2k     Lexical … Spreadshee…
#>  9 9100037                                 3 task-ld2k     Lexical … Spreadshee…
#> 10 9100037                                 3 task-ld2k     Lexical … Spreadshee…
#> # ℹ 30 more rows
#> # ℹ 15 more variables: spreadsheet_index <dbl>, display <chr>, trial <dbl>,
#> #   screen <chr>, screen_id <chr>, file <chr>, type <chr>, timestamp <dbl>,
